edition2026.description: Eight years of Chaotic-AUR: a timeline from 2018 until today and fun facts from our commit history
edition2026.keywords: Chaotic-AUR, Repository, Packages, Archlinux, AUR, Arch User Repository, Chaotic, Chaotic-AUR birthday, Chaotic-AUR history, Chaotic-AUR memorial
edition2026.subtitle: Since {{year}}, a team of volunteers pre-builds AUR packages for you. Here is how we got here.

timeline.infra1: infra 1.0 goes live with the first build scripts, repoctl and static pages.
timeline.ipfs: The repository becomes an IPFS peer. The experiment ends six weeks later.
timeline.tkg: The TkG kernels join the repository.
timeline.architectures: Support for other architectures and Arch-based distributions arrives.
timeline.firstMirror: BangL hosts the first community mirror.
timeline.zst: All packages switch to zstd compression.
timeline.interfere: The interfere repository starts to fix broken AUR packages.
timeline.garuda: Chaotic-AUR starts to build the Garuda Linux packages.
timeline.toolbox: The toolbox (infra 2.0) starts. The packages repository opens for issues.
timeline.infra1Death: “Last commit and the death of infra1.0”
timeline.infra3: Infra 3.0 brings routines, the keyring and the cleanup tools.
timeline.ufscar: The UFSCar HPC cluster joins as a builder.
timeline.router: The mirror router goes live on Heroku, together with the website at chaotic.cx.
timeline.syncthing: Mirrors start to sync with Syncthing.
timeline.realtimeMetrics: The router counts downloads in real time, with the country of each download.
timeline.silkyNetwork: The Silky Network begins providing many new mirrors for Chaotic-AUR.
timeline.geoRouting: Mirror health checks and geo routing send each user to a near, healthy mirror.
timeline.memorial3: The community celebrates the 3rd birthday with the first memorial.
timeline.dockerMirror: A Docker setup makes it easy to host a mirror.
timeline.ansible: An Ansible role bootstraps the primary node and the cluster nodes.
timeline.multiRepoRouter: The router supports more than one repository on the same mirror network.
timeline.mirrorMap: The first mirror map goes live.
timeline.r2Cdn: A Cloudflare R2 CDN mirror joins the network.
timeline.nyx: Chaotic-Nyx brings the idea to NixOS.
timeline.pkgrelIncrementer: The pkgrel incrementer rebuilds Haskell packages when their dependencies change.
timeline.infra4: Chaotic-AUR 4.0 moves the builds to GitLab CI.
timeline.toolboxEnd: The toolbox gets its last commit.
timeline.homeMap: The mirror map and the deployment log arrive on the website.
timeline.memorial6: The community celebrates the 6th birthday with the second memorial.
timeline.repoManager: Download metrics, the repo manager for automatic rebuilds and the TypeScript router arrive.
timeline.primeng: The website gets its first big rework.
timeline.humanReview: Active human review starts: major updates from AUR maintainers outside our trusted list get reviewed by a human before the merge.
timeline.flyio: The router moves from Heroku to fly.io.
timeline.highCaution: High caution mode: the trusted list is switched off. From now on, every major AUR update gets reviewed by a human before the merge.
timeline.optimus: Angular 22, AUR scans and failure tags arrive.
timeline.ghaBuilders: GitHub Actions runners join as extra build nodes.
timeline.uiRework: Another UI rework of the website, including SSG and multi-language support, just in time for the 8th birthday.
